subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should memory-core dreaming enforce per-agent isolation by default for shared workspaces, accept only an opt-in dreaming.agents allowlist, or document workspace-level pooling as expected behavior?
rationale: The current issue is source-reproducible and security-sensitive, but the durable boundary affects existing shared-workspace deployments, generated dream artifacts, and plugin config/API shape, so a maintainer should choose the product/security contract before repair work continues.

options.title: Default Agent Isolation
options.body: Treat workspace-level pooling as a bug and require the fix to isolate session ingestion, corpus, recall, promotion, and repair behavior per current agent.

options.title: Scoped Config Allowlist
options.body: Accept a PR like https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 as the initial mitigation while leaving explicit follow-up for full shared-workspace isolation.

options.title: Document Workspace Pooling
options.body: Reclassify shared workspace dreaming as intentionally shared memory and update docs/config guidance instead of changing runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Default Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Treat workspace-level pooling as a bug and require the fix to isolate session ingestion, corpus, recall, promotion, and repair behavior per current agent.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the current assignee and already narrowed the live issue to the shared-workspace isolation question.
